findings: l.915 existence is false as written: the inclusion of ℂ ∖ {1/(n+1)} into ℂ is a spread (Hausdorff, second countable, locally path-connected source, GX.locPathConnectedSpace_compl_countable) with NO completion in the paper's sense (GX.not_exists_isSpreadCompletion_foxSeq; in every universe: GX.not_isSpreadCompletion_foxSeq, and in general GX.not_isSpreadCompletion_of_not_isOpen): by uniqueness every completion is id_ℂ, and the image ℂ ∖ {1/(n+1)} is not open (0 is a limit of removed points). What is true: Fox's completion (space of ends) always exists with a dense, locally-connected-in image (Fox's own notion; IsFoxCompletion), and it is a completion in the paper's sense iff that image is open (GX.exists_isSpreadCompletion_iff) — e.g. when p lands in an open subset of its ordinary locus (the completion of a covering of a portly subset, the case l.1147/l.1170/l.1439 use).
l.915 uniqueness holds, in the strong form: any two completions (even in Fox's sense) are isomorphic by a UNIQUE homeomorphism over Y and under X (GX.IsFoxCompletion.existsUnique_homeomorph).

l.915 'fully faithful' is false (as the 2021 draft): the completion functor is faithful but not full (GX.not_full_foxCompletionFunctor: ℂ∖{0} and ℂ∖{1} both complete to ℂ, and the identity between the completions extends no morphism ℂ∖{0} → ℂ∖{1}; also GX.completion_not_full for the paper's completions id_ℂ). What l.1170 and l.1439 actually use is true and proved: every spread morphism (f, g) extends uniquely and continuously to the completions (GX.SpreadEnd.map, GX.SpreadEnd.eq_map), functorially (map_id, map_comp), and the extension determines g (map_injective); the same holds between ARBITRARY completions (Fox's or the paper's), as l.1170/l.1439 use it (GX.IsFoxCompletion.existsUnique_extend: a unique continuous ḡ with p₂'∘ḡ = f∘p₁' and ḡ∘ι₁ = ι₂∘g).

Local path-connectedness of the completion (needed for 'completion is a functor from Spread to itself' under the §3 standing assumptions, and used by lem:complete_path_carac l.1033 via lem:path_covering on the completion) is proved: GX.SpreadEnd.locPathConnectedSpace (paths to an end are infinite concatenations through e(W_n), W_n a decreasing basis at the base).
questions: The paper's 'completion of spread is a functor from Spread to itself' needs a locally connected base for the space of ends to be a spread; the functor is formalized on the full subcategory LocallyConnectedSpace Y ∧ T2Space Y ∧ T0Space X (the §3 standing assumptions imply it). Is that the intended domain?

hypotheses.paper: 𝓤 a connected neighbourhood basis of b
hypotheses.note: read as a family of OPEN connected neighbourhoods (IsCNbhd) forming a basis of 𝓝 b for the comparison with ends and the completeness criteria; the embedding and the image criterion are ALSO proved under the widest reading, 𝓤 any family of neighbourhoods of b (neither open nor connected) forming a basis (GX.fiberMapNhds, GX.isEmbedding_fiberMapNhds, GX.mem_range_fiberMapNhds_iff; equal to fiberMap on open connected ones by rfl)
T1Space Y for the surjectivity criteria, LocallyConnectedSpace Y for 'iff complete'

findings: l.928 'injective open': injective and an embedding (open onto its image) is proved (GX.isEmbedding_fiberMap); the literal 'open map into the inverse limit' is equivalent to the image being open (GX.isOpenMap_fiberMap_iff) and is FALSE, proved by GX.not_isOpenMap_fiberMap_comb: X = GX.combSet ⊆ ℝ², the x-axis with the arms {(t, r_n − t) : 0 < t ≤ r_n}, r_n = 2⁻ⁿ (Hausdorff, second countable, locally path-connected — instance), p = first projection (a spread, GX.isSpread_combProj), b = 0, 𝓤 = {(−ρ, ρ)}: p⁻¹(0) is the origin, and the arm-n thread (GX.combThread) agrees with the origin's on every (−ρ, ρ) with ρ > r_n (combThread_eq_of_lt) but is unrealised (combThread_ne), so every cylinder around φ(origin) leaves the image. The proof's identity φ(V ∩ p⁻¹(b)) = π_U⁻¹(V) (l.940) holds only when every thread through V is realised.

l.929 'homeomorphism iff complete' is false for a fixed b: exp : ℝ → ℝ at b = 1 has the natural map a homeomorphism for every basis while exp is not complete (GX.fiberMap_exp_bijective_not_complete). True forms: for fixed b, onto iff every thread (equivalently every end at b) has a point (surjective_fiberMap_iff_threads, surjective_fiberMap_iff_ends); complete iff onto for every b and every basis (GX.isCompleteSpread_iff_forall_surjective_fiberMap), equivalently for one basis at each b (GX.isCompleteSpread_iff_forall_exists_surjective_fiberMap), and then a homeomorphism (GX.fiberHomeomorph).
questions: Is 'injective open' meant as 'a homeomorphism onto its image' (proved) rather than 'an open map into the limit' (false, comb)?

Is 'connected neighbourhood basis' meant to allow non-open connected neighbourhoods? The comparison with ends is stated for open ones (IsCNbhd); the embedding is proved for any neighbourhood basis (fiberMapNhds).

kb_proposals: Fox completion = SpreadEnd p: a structure with base and a TOTAL toFun : Set Y → Set X normalised to ∅ off the connected open neighbourhoods; then equality of ends is plain structure ext (no dependent types), which made every comparison map easy.

The neighbourhood basis of an end e is basicSet W (e W), W a connected open nbhd of e.base; the only non-trivial fact is that basicSet W (e W) is the component of base⁻¹(W) (partition into the open sets basicSet W D).
Uniqueness of completions needs only dense + locally-connected-in image (Fox's notion), never openness; openness of the image is exactly the existence obstruction in the paper's definition.
ℂ minus a countable set: balls stay (path-)connected via OpenPartialHomeomorph.univBall + Set.Countable.isPathConnected_compl_of_one_lt_rank; open connected sets via GX.isPreconnected_of_local.

Elaboration pitfall: lemmas whose hypothesis is IsCNbhd (p x) U can unify p x with SpreadEnd.base e (p := base); pass (p := p) (x := x) explicitly. connectedComponentIn_subset _ _ h also mis-unifies; give F and x.

Local path-connectedness of a space of ends: chain paths through e(W_n) for a decreasing basis W_n := connectedComponentIn (interior (s n) ∩ W) base and close with GX.Path.exists_infConcat; the infConcat's 'every point before 1 is on some φ n' clause gives containment in the basic set.

Separating components of p⁻¹ V in a concrete subspace: IsPreconnected.subset_left_of_subset_union with two globally disjoint open sets of the subspace defined by continuous coordinate functions; isolate a discrete set of values (arm heights) by an open interval to get openness.
Path-connected subsets of a subtype S ⊆ ℝ²: prove it for the image set in ℝ² and pull back with IsInducing.subtypeVal.isPathConnected_iff + Subtype.image_preimage_coe.

To make a functor C ⥤ Spread into an endofunctor of a full subcategory P, use P.lift F hF (ObjectProperty.lift); Faithful transfers by instance, and ¬Full transfers via (P.lift F hF ⋙ P.ι = F) := rfl.
